import io

    "Beagle", "Deutsche Dogge", "Continental Bulldog", "Shiba Inu", "Cocker Spaniel"
]

years = list(range(2015, 2024))

data = []

        )[0],
        "AlterVHundNum": random.randint(0, 15)
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(15).sort_values(ascending=False)

# 2. Set up the plot style and figure

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 9))

    x=top_breeds.values,
    y=top_breeds.index,
    palette='viridis_r',
    ax=ax
)

# 4. Customize titles and labels for clarity and impact
fig.suptitle(
    'Top 15 Most Popular Dog Breeds',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    y=0.96
)

    'Based on a sample of 5,000 registered dogs (2015-2023)',
    fontsize=12,
    style='italic',
    pad=10
)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# 5. Add data labels to the end of each bar for precise reading
for p in ax.patches:
    width = p.get_width()
    ax.text(
        width + 10,  # Position label slightly to the right of the bar
        p.get_y() + p.get_height() / 2.,
        f'{int(width)}',
        ha='left',
        va='center',
        fontsize=10,
        color='black'
    )

# 6. Refine the plot's aesthetics
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_linewidth(0.5)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_linewidth(0.5)
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=11)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='y', b=False) # Remove horizontal grid lines
